land.text: Greater Poland, the base of Stanisław Leszczyński's confederation ('He had earlier organized a confederation in Greater Poland'); the Warsaw confederation of January-February 1704 declared Augustus II 'no longer king of Poland'

predecessors.note: The faction split the Commonwealth into a Swedish-backed and a Saxon-backed party; the loyalists (the Sandomierz Confederation) stayed with the Commonwealth row.

land.text: the 1706-1708 extent of the Swedish-backed Poland, returned to the rule of Augustus II when 'Augustus II returned to the throne' after Poltava

successors.note: The Stanisław page's infobox ends his first reign on 8 July 1709. Cliopatria carries a 758,657 km2 'Pro-Swedish Poland' shape to 1712 that is really the whole restored Commonwealth; see keyframe 1709 and notes.

capitals.name: Warsaw
capitals.note: The page names Warsaw only as the seat of the confederation ('A confederation in Warsaw between January and February 1704'); the Stanisław page names no capital for the first reign and has him living at Rydzyna after Poltava.

rulers.name: Stanisław I Leszczyński
rulers.title: King of Poland and Grand Duke of Lithuania (first reign)
rulers.note: Infobox '1st reign: 12 July 1704 – 8 July 1709' (the invasion page gives the election as 2 July 1704); crowned 24 September 1705 in the text, 4 October 1705 in the infobox; second reign 12 September 1733 – 26 January 1736 (not this state).

correction.text: Greater Poland, 'the base' of the confederation that elected Stanisław: 'He had earlier organized a confederation in Greater Poland'; 'During 1705 the faction supporting Stanisław and the Swedes grew considerably'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts this row in 1706, but the Warsaw confederation deposed Augustus in January-February 1704 and Leszczyński was elected in July 1704. The page names Greater Poland (and Toruń, taken by Charles XII) but not the extent he controlled, so the keyframe is only the core; Cliopatria draws the whole Commonwealth as one row in 1702-1705.

Unverified: page budget. 348,691 km2 (bbox 15.49-27.09E, 49.05-57.83N, Poland, Lithuania, Belarus), of which Greater Poland (123 of its 126 cells) is inside. Neither page gives the extent Stanisław controlled or an area. Cliopatria's 1706 start coincides with the Altranstädt peace of 14 September 1706 ('Augustus renounced his claims to the Polish throne'); the Commonwealth row keeps 436,745 km2 beside it in 1706-1708 (Cliopatria's split of the Commonwealth between the two parties), and the page says Charles XII then turned to 'chasing the Russians out of eastern Poland'.

correction.text: for 1709 only (to 8 July 1709) use the 1706-1708 extent; there is no pro-Swedish state afterwards: 'Augustus II returned to the throne' after the defeat at Poltava, so the whole 1709-1712 shape is the restored Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth

keyframe_review.note: 758,657 km2 (bbox 15.49-32.82E, 47.27-57.83N, Poland, Ukraine, Belarus): the 1706 Pro-Swedish extent plus 446,874 km2 of the Commonwealth's other half (the 1706 Commonwealth row east of it). The Stanisław page ends his first reign on 8 July 1709 and says the Poltava defeat of Charles XII restored Augustus, so labelling the whole Commonwealth 'pro-Swedish' to 1712 is wrong. Cliopatria's Commonwealth row for 1709-1712 is a 32,670 km2 piece in Germany and Poland (bbox 10.10-15.27E, 50.25-52.25N), which the polish-lithuanian-commonwealth dossier should replace.

region.text: Greater Poland, where Stanisław 'had earlier organized a confederation'

ledger.note: 1704: a Swedish-backed assembly elects Stanisław Leszczyński king of Poland-Lithuania. 'A confederation in Warsaw between January and February 1704 declared that king Augustus was no longer king of Poland'; the councillors 'could safely elect Stanisław Leszczyński as king of Poland–Lithuania on 2 July 1704' (the Stanisław page gives 12 July 1704, 'election by a scratch assembly of half a dozen castellans and a few score of noblemen', and the infobox the same). Only the base, Greater Poland, is named.

region.text: Greater Poland, which Augustus tried 'to use military force to keep ... down'

ledger.note: 28 October 1704: the first dated battle of the new regime, Poniec. 'Charles XII fought the Battle of Poniec on 28 October 1704' (the page's date; it does not describe the ground); Augustus tried 'to use military force to keep Greater Poland down' and its officials 'refused to accept him as king' (undated). The contest is between the Swedish-backed faction and the king's party, the Sandomierz Confederation and Saxony, which the Commonwealth row carries.

region.text: the rest of the 1706 extent beyond Greater Poland: 'During 1705 the faction supporting Stanisław and the Swedes grew considerably'

ledger.note: 1706 (Cliopatria's first shape year): the Swedish-backed Poland spreads beyond Greater Poland. The page says the faction 'grew considerably' in 1705 and that Stanisław signed the Treaty of Warsaw with Sweden in 1705, but it names no further land; the region is Cliopatria's 1706 shape beyond Greater Poland (page silent).

14 September 1706: Augustus II renounces the Polish throne at Altranstädt. Charles XII 'enforced the peace of Altranstädt on 14 September 1706, in which Augustus renounced his claims to the Polish throne'. The page has Augustus recognise Stanisław as ruler; fighting against Augustus's Polish supporters and the Russians in eastern Poland continued (the page: Charles XII 'could now concentrate on chasing the Russians out of eastern Poland').

July 1709: Stanisław loses the throne after Poltava and Augustus returns. 'In 1709, Charles XII of Sweden, Stanisław's main supporter, suffered a defeat by the Russians at the Battle of Poltava' and 'As a result, Augustus II returned to the throne'; the infobox ends the first reign on 8 July 1709. The page gives no territorial detail.

region.text: the Swedish-backed Poland of Stanisław I

ledger.note: 8 July 1709: Stanisław's first reign ends and the Swedish-backed regime with it; he went to Swedish Pomerania and later lived at Rydzyna (page, undated). Infobox: '1st reign: 12 July 1704 – 8 July 1709'.

wars.name: Swedish invasion of Poland (1701–1706)

zones.text: Greater Poland, the base of the Warsaw confederation

wars.outcome: 'Swedish-led victory': the Warsaw confederation deposed Augustus in 1704, Stanisław Leszczyński was elected and, after the Swedish victories (Wschowa/Fraustadt, Toruń), Augustus renounced his claim at Altranstädt on 14 September 1706.
wars.note: Infobox sides: Swedish Empire and Warsaw Confederation against Saxony, Sandomierz Confederation, Russia and Cossack Hetmanate; the Commonwealth's loyalist party is mapped to polish-lithuanian-commonwealth. The page covers events only to 1708 and dates few battles.

wars.name: Battle of Poltava
wars.outcome: Charles XII, Stanisław's main supporter, was defeated by the Russians; 'As a result, Augustus II returned to the throne' and Stanisław's first reign ended on 8 July 1709.
wars.note: Listed for its effect on this state; the Stanisław page mentions the battle only in a sentence. No territorial zone.

certainty.note: A Swedish-backed faction's holdings in a civil war; no treaty or survey line, and neither page names the extent held.

notes: Written by eu-15-k on 2026-10-25 from two pages (page budget 1-2). (1) The Cliopatria row 1706-1712 is two shapes: 1706-1708 (348,691 km2) beside a 436,745 km2 Commonwealth row, and 1709-1712 (758,657 km2) that is the entire Commonwealth. The second is wrong (keyframe verdict wrong); the polish-lithuanian-commonwealth dossier should note that its 1709-1712 row (32,670 km2, Saxon lands) is not the Commonwealth and that the restored Commonwealth under Augustus II is what Cliopatria labels 'Pro-Swedish Poland'. (2) State TYPE: given as state because Augustus recognised Stanisław at Altranstädt (14 September 1706) and Cliopatria draws it as a polity; the colour agent may treat 1704-1706 as a rebel faction (hatched) if it prefers rule 5. (3) No page opened gives the extent held by Stanisław; the 1704-1705 keyframe is the Greater Poland core only, and the 1706 shape is unverified. The Great Northern War page, Altranstädt page and the Sandomierz Confederation would settle it. The Russians' eastern Poland, the Treaty of Warsaw (1705) and the Swedish occupation of 1706-1708 are not dated by the pages opened. (4) The two pages disagree on the election (2 July against 12 July 1704) and on the coronation (September against 4 October 1705); the dossier month is July. (5) The Saxon-Polish loyalists (Sandomierz Confederation, Augustus II) have no dossier of their own; they are the polish-lithuanian-commonwealth row. 'Cossack Hetmanate' is the infobox's name for Mazepa's side and is left as a name in wars[].belligerents. No gazetteer names unknown.
